prompt: A flat layered paper-cut collage in a strict handcraft design system: everything is cut from colored cardstock and hanji paper with perfectly clean cut edges — NO outline of any kind on any piece: no bright edge line, no white edge, no dark contour line. Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. A premium paper-art illustration in the style of a recessed layered paper frame (like looking through a porthole cut into thick paper): SIX to EIGHT concentric paper frame layers step inward, each layer a slightly different shade, casting soft shadows inward, forming a deep tunnel; inside the tunnel a small detailed paper-cut scene. Some elements of the story break OUT over the front frame edge for extra depth. The whole piece sits on a plain textured cream paper background with generous margin. Cute Korean picture-book style for 3-4 year olds. The frame opening is a round green lily pad with its little notch, frame layers stepping from deep pond green to lime to pale mint. Inside: a sunny pond meadow with reeds, a huge gentle brown ox standing far back in the grass. Breaking out over the front edge: a chubby green mother frog puffing up her round belly proudly, and two tiny baby frogs sitting on the rim, a few water droplets spilling out. No text.

Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. A premium paper-art illustration in the style of a recessed layered paper frame (like looking through a porthole cut into thick paper): SIX to EIGHT concentric paper frame layers step inward, each layer a slightly different shade, casting soft shadows inward, forming a deep tunnel; inside the tunnel a small detailed paper-cut scene. Some elements of the story break OUT over the front frame edge for extra depth. The whole piece sits on a plain textured cream paper background with generous margin. Cute Korean picture-book style for 3-4 year olds. The frame opening is a round Korean temple bell shape, frame layers stepping from bronze to warm gold to cream. Inside: a misty Korean mountain with pine trees and a small temple at dusk. Breaking out over the front edge: a black-and-white magpie with a long tail flying out over the rim, and a gentle young scholar in hanbok looking up. No text.
